newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SEE AIRBUS AS WAY TO RETAIN AEROSPACE SKILLS.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SEE AIRBUS AS WAY TO RETAIN AEROSPACE SKILLS.

text.p: As bankrupt Fokker NV edges ever closer to liquidation, Dutch businessmen and politicians say that a role in the European Airbus consortium could be the best way to preserve the country's aerospace skills.
Foremost among those advocating the "Airbus option" is Jan Hovers, chairman of Stork NV which acquired Fokker's profitable aircraft component and maintenance units in July.
Hovers told Dutch television Fokker's demise, after rescue talks with South Korea's Samsung Aerospace broke down last week, did not mean the loss of Dutch aerospace expertise.
"We certainly think that...we have the ingredients to play an important role in the aerospace industry in Europe, and I hope worldwide," he said.

In addition to the businesses now grouped in Stork's Fokker Aviation subsidiary, valuable Dutch aerospace know-how also resided with the national aerospace institute (NIVR) and at the aeronautics department of Delft technical university, he said.
A good way of putting this knowledge to work, he said, was through the Airbus consortium which currently comprises aircraft builders from Germany, France, Britain and Spain.
Hovers said Fokker Aviation already supplied wing components for some Airbus aircraft but would like to play a larger role within the consortium.
In particular, Hovers said he hoped to obtain development funds from the national aerospace institute so Fokker Aviation could help build the Airbus A3XX "superjumbo".
"The idea would be that we get money from the NIVR to finance the development of our part of the A3XX programme, the 600-seater Airbus," he said.
The development grants would be repaid from revenues once the planes were being produced, he added.
Daan Krook, a senior manager at Fokker until 1988 and vice-president of Airbus from 1975 to 1979, urged the Dutch to forge close ties with Airbus.
"Whether or not the bankrupt Fokker gets taken over by Samsung, I think we should consider participation in Airbus again," he told the NRC Handelsblad newspaper.
Fokker had modest stakes in the early A300 and A310 Airbus programmes but did not take part in later programmes.
Member of parliament Jan van Walsem said a stake in Airbus would give an important boost to Dutch high-tech firms.
"Participation in Airbus would benefit many companies. We would get lots of offset orders which would stimulate high-quality employment and new technologies," he said.
Minister of Economic Affairs Hans Wijers has said the government is willing to consider providing financial support for a Dutch role in Airbus if Fokker is liquidated.

That prospect had become increasingly likely, he said, now that Short Brothers had stopped supplying wings, forcing Fokker's court-appointed administrators to end exclusive takeover talks with Samsung.
